sentences.text: None for the applicant even in second round.
Shri J.M. Sahani, Panel Lawyer for the State/respondent.
The matter is pending since the year 2013 and it appears that learned counsel for the applicant is not interested to argue the matter.
Sometimes he appeared before the Court and sometimes he did not appear before the Court.
Heard the learned Panel Lawyer finally.

The applicant has preferred the present criminal revision against the judgment dated 29.05.2013 passed by the Sessions Judge, Bhind, in Criminal Appeal No. 379/2012, whereby the Sessions Judge has remanded the matter in which initially the JMFC passed the judgment dated 19.10.2012 in Criminal Case No. 1534/2006, whereby the applicant was convicted of offence under Section 16(1)(a)(1) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act and sentenced to two years rigorous imprisonment with fine of Rs.2,000/-.

Prosecution's case, in short, is that a sample of 'Khoya' was taken by the respondent - Food Inspector from the applicant and since it was found adulterated, the complaint was filed and trial was started.
The JMFC, Bhind in Criminal Case No. 1534/2006 passed the judgment dated 19.10.2012 whereby the applicant was convicted and sentenced as mentioned above.

He filed a Criminal Appeal No. 379/2012 and vide judgment dated 29.05.2013, the appellate Court remanded the matter with the direction that few charges be framed against the applicant and re-trial be done.

After considering the submissions made by the learned counsel for the State, it would be apparent that before the appellate Court, an appeal was filed by the applicant and, therefore, the appellate Court could not pass any order which was against the applicant himself.

If there was a defect of charge in the file by the trial Court then it was for the learned Sessions Judge to take suo moto revision against that order and an opportunity of hearing was to be given to the applicant separately and thereafter he could pass such an order to remand the case but instead of adopting such procedure, the learned Sessions Judge simply decided the appeal by remanding the case to the trial Court.
The judgment dated 29.05.2013 passed by the Sessions Judge, is beyond his jurisdiction when he did not take suo moto revision.

Under these circumstances, looking to the perversity and refusal of adopting the correct procedure,
it is a fit case in which revisionary power of this Court may be exercised.
Consequently, revision filed by the applicant - Puttu Singh is hereby allowed.

The judgment dated 29.05.2013 passed by the Sessions Judge, Bhind is hereby set aside with the direction that Criminal Appeal No. 379/2012 is Puttu Singh vs State Of M.P. on 13 February, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/36551411/
1 restored to its original number and the Sessions Judge shall decide the appeal on merits of evidence available on record and if the Sessions Judge desires to remand the case for re-framing of the charges then a separate suo moto cognizance in criminal revision shall be taken by him before proceeding in Criminal Appeal No. 379/2012.
